findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] alternative-mitigation-accepted: lines 23-29 throttle the token endpoint with @limiter.limit('5/minute') placed directly beneath @router.post('/token'), in the required decorator order, and the handler takes request: Request so slowapi can hook in. The limiter is wired app-wide in init_app.py:193-194 (app.state.limiter plus the RateLimitExceeded handler, so over-limit calls return 429) and rate_limiting.py:32 sets default_limits=['120/minute'] so no route is unthrottled by omission. The client key (rate_limiting.py:9-27) prefers the subject of a signature-verified JWT and only falls back to slowapi get_remote_address, which reads request.client.host rather than a spoofable forwarded header - addressing the fabricated-identity evasion in the weakness description. Brute force is additionally bounded by the lockout module: seconds_remaining/register_failure/register_success gate the login, and a locked identity receives byte-identical 401 output with no 429 or Retry-After, so the throttle itself is not an oracle. One residual item from the recommendation is outside this file: the Limiter is constructed without a storage_uri, so counters are per-process and will not hold across workers or replicas until a shared Redis/Memcached store is configured. Recorded as informational; the endpoint-level throttle the CM requires is present. | verdict=pass confidence=high
